speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when you first noticed this painful ulcer on your leg and if you have a history of diabetes or poor circulation?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease, the painful ulcer could be pyoderma gangrenosum, but I need to rule out infection. Do you have any other symptoms such as fever, joint pain, or changes in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of pitting edema and dilated tortuous veins strongly suggests underlying venous insufficiency. To confirm this and rule out other causes, I will order a lower extremity venous duplex ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: Lower_extremity_venous_duplex_ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal venous ultrasound, the edema and varicose veins appear incidental to the ulcer's etiology. The history of an ant bite triggering a painful ulcer with purplish borders in a patient with Crohn's disease strongly suggests Pyoderma Gangrenosum, but I must rule out infection. REQUEST TEST: Wound_culture_and_biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Wound culture: Negative for bacterial growth. Skin biopsy histopathology: Neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.
